info.title: Connect canonical HTTP commands
info.description: Current isolated local macOS arm64 control surface. POST a normative unsigned UCTP v2 envelope using an explicit current bearer. Native QUIC and HTTP use the same service parsers, result builders, current Store policy and durable operation ledger. This is not a signed physical-peer grant and never falls back to another dialect. General Session/media installation and Linux/remote/browser operating profiles remain their assigned work. Protected optional public assistant hosting can react to an AI participant's own committed session.accept. The Session receipt confirms admission, not provider context delivery or media readiness. No HTTP command installs a provider profile or grants model execution authority. Canonical server TOML can select protected public native Vapi hosts. Named participant routing and capability reads use the same constructed Endpoint and current credential/key bindings; sharing a transport or secret reference does not configure an unrelated Endpoint. These configuration facts do not assert provider reachability.

post.description: Installed: conversation.create/list/get/close/subscribe (finite HTTP catch-up with explicit live:false), record discovery through conversation.get record items and recording.vcon-ready hints on finite catch-up (current record_get plus Session source access; pending/ready/unavailable metadata, UUID/revision only; recording.vcon-fetch uses an explicit closing HTTP/1.1 response with current bearer/source/record custody through actual socket IO; inline views up to128KiB, exact projected digest and conditional reads; HTTP/2/upgrades refused; larger views use the optional pinned authenticated expiring HTTPS endpoint), participant.add/update/remove, message.send/history/read, operation.get/cancel/reconcile, session.consult/handoff, session.consult.return and connection.replace durable admission (current original source/provisioned-endpoint metadata, bounded independent physical preparation authority and once-only durable actual Core preparation are installed for live native QUIC or established provisioned telephone sources and independently signed native targets; original audio/roles remain intact and cancel/current authority loss releases the owned preparation; independently signed native targets allocate the exact Core reservation once through the public SDK, negotiate generation-two resources, attach a closed muted private audience and prove actual discarded input plus completed local output while public media stays closed. the native continuation now performs one actual managed movement after current private duplex readiness and configured native confirmation, carries exact existing resource confirmation and adopts the actual committed next-generation binding. Schema58 records independent target lifetime, old-only retirement, topology, journal and captured audience stream revisions so later controls stay current. Original execution/source revocation cannot end the established target, and current target loss cleans only its route. Provisioned telephone callback uses configured attributed answer-DTMF, real private duplex and one managed movement. Independent established SIP authority, PCMU/PCMA, ringing/private cancellation, voicemail/refused confirmation/deadline, discarded-response recovery, restart/drop fencing, selectors and mixed physical roles are locally qualified. A confirmed telephone source can move to a separately signed native target at the next lineage generation. Established refresh and rejected-refresh ACK preserve current duplex; replay cannot redial. Browser/remote/provider and the wider fault matrix remain assigned integration qualifications.), general session.invite/accept/reject/cancel/update/end control, including explicit existing-Session invitations, scoped appearance/role decisions and unconnected capability changes. Consult admission excludes the retained remote from its private participant set, requires an explicit primary to be private, and recognizes native ready routes only through their current confirmed original lifetime; initial admission alone performs no media IO. Once a trusted registered private candidate completes signed muted preparation, exact authenticated replay can queue one actual private audio audience application and silent remote hold. Native human completion additionally requires actual decoded audio, exact private preparation and current physical incarnations. Its atomic local commit installs a separate active private lifetime, increments the Session topology revision once and releases the execution lease. Current peer credentials, Devices, Endpoints and original membership epochs govern established media independently of the original execution credential. The named session.consult.return permission admits a new operation bound to the original consultation record, explicit primary and retained remote at the current Session revision. Its fresh current native scene authorizes one actual restoration using the original scene-issued handle. Confirmed restoration removes only the primary floor; private candidate content stays isolated and completion waits for its observed native retirement. The result reports retained/retired Connections, Session revision and remote_continuing; known remote EOF cannot assert a continuing call. Current authorization is checked on replay, which never repeats an attempted media effect. Schema52 adds an internal Store boundary for separately captured provider creation and context export: private JSON is unavailable before a unique fresh provider instance is recorded. AI audience preparation/begin and completion require independent confirmed context initialization, with decoded media still separately required. Private transcripts retain original Connection/audience provenance and public provider projections exclude them. These Store APIs are not public HTTP commands. The protected server library private Vapi bridge owns a fresh signed native peer, separate actual HTTP/WebSocket call, exact-message context acknowledgment and PCMU forwarding, with current history policy independently gating native candidate packets. Its designated local provider fixtures are separate from live-provider qualification. The installed stock automatic coordinator has separate configuration and qualification records. Internal native consultation audience effects reserve one exact plan and attempt; a confirmed audience application is not consulting audio readiness or operation completion. HTTP exposes current authorized status/cancellation, not a native worker permit. Trusted native consultation invitation registration now pins a fresh candidate context before allocation; its signed offer is muted and quarantined before managed scene publication. This audio-only preparation precedes the private audience switch; it is not consulting readiness or provider initialization. The primary private original-audience floor is installed before audience IO, legacy whole-Session provider transcript/context paths permanently require Connection-bound context after a private candidate exists, and actual media interruption preserves known applied effects and private floors. Decoded audio is separate historical progress; a native human can complete only through the verified active-lifetime commit. AI roots remain preparing without a result until fresh private provider context is ready. A competing consultation cannot adopt an occupied private slot. Native connection.offer, connection.end, connection.update(codec-renegotiate), stream.subscribe/unsubscribe and Session/Connection-scoped message.send require their actual signed native QUIC or configured WebTransport physical peer and return explicit 501 unsupported responses over HTTP; current operation status and cancellation remain available here. Explicit screen acceptance and additive upgrades use their own VP8 capability intersection; video permission does not grant screen. Accepted additive media upgrades may retain settled current native Connections; actual new media still requires signed native Connection negotiation. Reliable data uses the Session reliable-ordered delivery class with separately negotiated native formats; trusted admission now retains one durable message and original audience, with exact signed physical-source/active-format preflight, one Core queue publication, fresh original-message/audience authorization and reserved historical local writer facts. Native text/json/binary formats are installed; local writes and crash uncertainty never assert remote consumption. Participant camera/screen/data selectors and automatic signed native reoffers are installed. Server materialization has an internal stream.reconcile operation record with its subscription_record_id, server_reconciliation marker and actual local outcome; current operation status/cancellation are available here, but stream.reconcile is not an accepted wire/HTTP command. Signed native connection.update(codec-renegotiate) requires separate current connection.update permission, the original physical peer, current accepted Session/endpoint/profile capabilities and exact stream revision. Actual negotiated codec bindings and the resulting stream revision are historical observations; replay never reapplies native work. Other connection.update actions remain explicit unsupported commands under their assigned tasks. Terminal ended/rejected/cancelled/failed Session state releases its native runtime; persistent Conversations close only by explicit policy when active work has ended. Accepted optional transition payload fields remain in the original durable digest, including nested values, array order and explicit nulls; changed or omitted extensions conflict under the same operation ID. The original-private-human-target native handoff profile now uses actual managed participant/media commit for observe or leave, retains the remote Connection and applies current per-physical-peer audio authority after commit. Session scope changes that engagement; Conversation scope also changes the two role defaults. The signed native target-owned connect-handoff-preparation-v1 audio profile now permits current named session.handoff holders to prepare their own muted, closed Connection before any caller handoff exists. Its immutable signed offer record is the later policy_ref; it grants neither decoded readiness nor role promotion. Human, AI and Observer preparation retain their current roles. HTTP connection.offer remains unsupported. Generic prepared native human/AI takeover is installed: the server captures the real closed admission, decodes and discards isolated input under a separate current grant, and generates neutral silence through its exact negotiated codec and guarded writer. Actual duplex IO mints sealed readiness; the preparation receipt or enqueued output cannot substitute. The managed role/media commit consumes that exact capability and unmutes only the incoming Connection, including atomic promotion of an initially Observer audio consumer. Four actual native scenarios qualify both identity directions, observe/Session and leave/Conversation scope with retained remote/Main Session and one attempt. A bounded owned wait retries planning-only readiness misses under fresh current authority, without holding readers or role fences while idle; late target input can complete the original request without replay. An occupied transition footprint refuses competing admission before ledger effects. Actual public native checks cover cancellation before IO, controller revocation with original duplex preserved, fresh same-owner source recovery for the same unchanged-expiry intention, and stale topology refusal. Repeated distinct handoffs consume the current scene-issued audience by committed source membership and audience revision. Prior observers are closed out unless selected by the new audience, and metadata follows the latest applied receiver programme. Still-closed independent preparations obtain fresh actual output after another audience commit invalidates old readiness; the bounded worker retains no idle grant. Completed operation replay never restores an earlier audience. This native endpoint qualification does not assert opaque provider-memory freshness; remaining failure/recovery and remote-profile qualification stay explicit. Definitive preflight refusal before any native effect records failed with an attributable problem and preserves the original private audio/hold; status and replay retain the same problem. This refusal cannot settle prepared or possibly submitted work, and missing decoded audio is not a definitive policy refusal. Preserve original logical IDs across uncertainty. ACK terminates the response, not media or asynchronous work. Old canonical Operation bodies and transport signatures are refused. Named application/admin/task APIs remain independently scoped.

200.description: Correlated canonical reply envelopes through ACK.

400.description: Malformed request or bounded application refusal.

401.description: Current bearer expired, revoked or invalid.

403.description: Current floor, recipient, Participant or resource authority refused.

404.description: Authorized record selector is unavailable; correlated recording error.

409.description: Original intent, revision or cursor conflicts.

429.description: Request capacity or bounded reply batch exhausted.

488.description: Requested media capabilities have no usable intersection.

501.description: Recognized but uninstalled command or unsupported HTTP live mode.

503.description: Authority or storage unavailable; retain the original logical ID.

x-connect-operation-recovery.target: Payload operation_id names the existing original operation; top-level operation_id names a separate stable cancel/reconcile decision.
x-connect-operation-recovery.authority: Current operation permission, original command/source authority, owner and recipient ceilings apply after restart and on replay.
x-connect-operation-recovery.evidence: Reconciliation references existing protected evidence bound to the current operation revision and worker generation. A caller-declared evidence ID or operator attestation cannot manufacture provider termination or physical completion.
x-connect-operation-recovery.retry: Preserve original logical IDs and unresolved conflicting reservations. A new ID does not authorize another external submission.

x-native-subscriptions.transport: Signed current original native QUIC peer only; HTTP may inspect operation outcomes but cannot install a native receive route.
x-native-subscriptions.selectors: Exact strm_id, from_participant, or from_participant with an explicit kinds list. Omitted kinds selects compatible declared receiver kinds within the installed profile, including later admitted sources of that pinned member epoch. A source supporting fewer kinds does not reject the wildcard when at least one kind is compatible and authorized. Unsupported source kinds remain future intent, without granting IO; explicit kinds are required exactly. It does not request unsupported screen/data or grant media capability.
x-native-subscriptions.authority: Current stream.subscribe, original Device/key/Connection, membership and source/recipient authorization remain required. Every future source and actual forwarding reacquires its own current authority.
x-native-subscriptions.unsubscribe: stream.unsubscribe strm_ids removes routes toward this Connection and records exceptions to retained Participant selectors. Exact replay returns the original outcome; a fresh repeated removal is a no-op with unchanged stream revision. Explicit resubscription clears the exception.
x-native-subscriptions.outcome: The shared operation ledger retains the exact original payload and expected revision. Successful selection terminates with ACK. Unknown current sources terminate with correlated error 404; incompatible media capabilities terminate with correlated error 488. A preceding operation.updated and operation.get retain the durable failed result. Exact replay returns that failure under current authorization. Refusal creates no native effect and does not partially install a mixed selector list.
x-native-subscriptions.metadata-capture: Native invocation target/source reads share one bounded Store connection interval and the original command authority. Validate the same original attempt before and after capture, retain each source audience/scope/expiry check, omit refused sources, and return no partial snapshot on other errors. Release SQL custody before Core or actual IO; do not create authority, repeat a routing effect or extend the command deadline.

x-native-active-speaker.emission: Disabled in the installed default profile; advisory hints are optional and never authority or durable Session state.
x-native-active-speaker.active_participant: Required Participant identifier or explicit null for silence/no dominant speaker; omission is invalid.

x-session-codec-preferences.admission: Current Session owner/manager, named permission and expected topology revision. Live targets require the installed bounded canonical codec worker.
x-session-codec-preferences.negotiation: New native offers use the latest Session preference order within current accepted Endpoint and Session capabilities and the original peer-offered formats; unavailable preferences fall back to usable peer order. The signed offer and advertised capabilities remain intact.
x-session-codec-preferences.replay: Original recorded outcome cannot reset newer preferences or existing bindings.
x-session-codec-preferences.live: The canonical Session codec worker uses fresh independently current actual signed native QUIC peer authority and exact prepared confirmation for each changed Connection. Per-peer unchanged selections retain bindings and revision. Inspect the separate reconciliation operation; policy completion does not imply completed media.

durable-reconciliation.availability: Installed in the running canonical runtime at schema98: at most16 concurrent jobs, fixed per-batch deadline up to30 seconds bounded by the initiating credential, durable polling and shutdown retirement. Without a running coordinator, live updates refuse explicitly. Native QUIC composition has its separately recorded local qualification; broader profiles remain assigned.
durable-reconciliation.policy-receipt: A live policy decision carries optional codec_reconciliation with a separate operation_id and record_id. The completed policy receipt does not claim completed physical changes.
durable-reconciliation.status: operation.get/cancel require current owner/member/management and original recipient authority. Pending, unknown and cancelled operations retain no completed result. A completed reconciliation reports aggregate durable outcomes, including partial refusals, without private Connection IDs.
durable-reconciliation.replay: Original policy and reference stay immutable. Superseded unstarted targets perform no IO; submitted effects retain uncertainty and never resubmit. Captured actual successes may record after cancellation without restoring an old policy.

x-owned-sdk-live-events.transport: The owned Rust SDK uses actual native conversation.subscribe live sources; HTTP live submission remains explicitly unsupported (501), with finite catch-up available by live:false.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.bootstrap: Without an explicit cursor, completely drain one pinned conversation.get snapshot (same revision/watermark) before opening live after that watermark. Bootstrap facts are metadata and cannot acquire native ownership.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.source: One source per Conversation and at most8 per physical Client. Requests have cid only, no logical operation ID or expected_revision. A10-second source lease renews through fresh current-authorized subscribe exchanges after the last complete ACK watermark. The application cursor advances only for facts returned to the caller, who persists it after actual processing.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.bounds: At most256 queued events and2MiB encoded journal payload per reader;256 immutable event identities deduplicate replay independently of opaque cursor token changes. Active/retired correlation tags are bounded to64. Capacity or retention loss never fabricates a successful catch-up.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.recovery: Full correlated ACK and matching outer/inner event identity, scope, kind and revision precede queue adoption. Failed/expired/resync sources clear unreturned facts and retain the last application boundary; create an explicit resumed/fresh reader. Malformed or refused source batches do not close unrelated healthy control. Physical signature/framing failures remain terminal.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.cancellation: Dropping a next wait preserves owned initialization and in-flight framing. Per-next timeout consumes no queued fact. Reader close/cancel stops local delivery and renewal; the existing bounded server lease expires without an invented unsubscribe command. Client close wakes all readers.
x-owned-sdk-live-events.native_journal_catch_up: Before returning a completed Operation journal fact for an owned native Session, the Rust event reader performs a bounded current-authorized original operation.get. Only exact issued-selector lineage and unchanged owned captured bindings can advance routing counters. A missing dedicated live hint needs no mutation replay or native parameter answer. Pending event bytes/count remain charged; cancellation or a refused/malformed current read retains the same fact and previous returned cursor. HTTP remains finite control catch-up and grants no physical native custody.

x-owned-sdk-incoming-invitations.native: The owned Rust Client receives actual signed server session.invite metadata on its existing peer; no media Connection, Conversation subscription or manually copied callee IDs are required. There is no HTTP push inbox or implicit transport downgrade.
x-owned-sdk-incoming-invitations.authority: The original server invitation source correlation, from/to Participants, medium, intent and capability offer are hints. The received operation_id is that stable source correlation, distinct from the caller private mutation ID and any separately saved decision mutation ID. Refresh current Session state before a separately identified ordinary session.accept/reject mutation; current membership/topology/source/action checks remain mandatory. Notification receipt never accepts or acquires media custody.
x-owned-sdk-incoming-invitations.bounds: One active reader per Client,32 queued hints,1MiB encoded invitation payload,256 immutable logical identities and four bounded cancellation correlations per identity. Duplicate original metadata is suppressed across fresh wire IDs; changed original metadata or malformed scope fails only the invitation inbox. Overflow explicitly requires authoritative resynchronization and cannot be cleared by merely reopening a reader.
x-owned-sdk-incoming-invitations.lifecycle: Per-wait deadlines/drop/cancellation consume no hint. Close/drop detaches the reader and preserves bounded pending hints for a replacement. Exact known signed cancellation removes only its pending scoped invitation. Client close clears bodies and wakes waits; other healthy control/media/event readers remain independent.

x-owned-sdk-runtime-capabilities.local: Rust Client.capabilities refreshes the local interface manifest of its actual owned connect/2 QUIC peer, without network IO, shared request slots or server policy refresh. RuntimeRole is Rust; selected_transport is QUIC and fallback_reason is absent. Optional receipt support reflects explicit application configuration.
x-owned-sdk-runtime-capabilities.require: Known feature names describe implemented interface support. Unknown/unavailable features return structured Unsupported. Invalid names/options, cancellation, expired authenticated lifetime and retired owners refuse without mutation or fabricated readiness.
x-owned-sdk-runtime-capabilities.boundary: Native programmatic media means bounded packet/data IO, not desktop capture, encoders, codec negotiation, actual decoded flow or provider delivery. Features do not discover routes, delegate permissions or install local media custody. Every actual action still requires current server policy and actual behavior evidence.

x-owned-sdk-receipts.configuration: Rust sdk.ClientConfig explicitly selects native control plus optional protected loopback application reads with the exact same credential; all config is checked before transport construction. Native Local/Remote trust remains explicit. No canonical HTTP fallback or remote HTTP trust is inferred.
x-owned-sdk-receipts.query: Conversation.receipts uses the existing named MessageReceipts application API, never a retired canonical operation. Every page requires current original-source membership/epoch, audience, permission and receipt preferences. Returned state retains Participant, membership epoch, channel, delivery identity, provenance and observed time; client_reported Read is not proof of human action.
x-owned-sdk-receipts.bounds: One independently owned serial HTTP reader with16 active/queued requests. All receipt pages share one absolute caller deadline, at most256 pages/4096 observations/2MiB encoded data,100 facts per page. Bad scope/provenance/counters, repeated cursors/groups and later refusal discard the accumulated result. Per-page current policy is not an atomic multi-page snapshot.
x-owned-sdk-receipts.lifecycle: Native control-only clients explicitly return Unsupported for receipt reads. Read cancellation disposes its separate HTTP transaction without changing original native mutation certainty. No new application read starts after native retirement. Client.close signals both owners and retains their joins across cleanup cancellation/timeouts. No implicit reporting or Message send occurs.

x-owned-sdk-raw-canonical.transport: Rust Client.raw uses its existing signed native peer and bounded owned request queue. No HTTP fallback or older dialect is selected.
x-owned-sdk-raw-canonical.validation: validate checks the current schema and one MiB envelope bound. Local validation is not signature verification, authorization or media ownership. to_json retains original optional fields; Debug omits private bodies.
x-owned-sdk-raw-canonical.request: Finite requests preserve complete payload extensions, scope, logical mutation ID and expected revision. Fresh physical ID, timestamp and signature replace attempt metadata. Unknown top-level intent fields refuse rather than silently dropping data. Mutations require a logical ID. Successful batches retain every signed correlated frame and terminal ACK. Canonical errors remain structured SDK errors.
x-owned-sdk-raw-canonical.recovery: Persist complete original intent/ID before IO. Started cancellation retains uncertainty and exchange ownership; operation.get reads the original without replay. Finite journal catch-up requires explicit live:false and caller-managed pagination/cursor.
x-owned-sdk-raw-canonical.lifecycle: Auth/step-up, native offer/answer/ready/ICE, binary record transfer, live leases and server-only replies require dedicated lifecycle helpers and refuse as standalone raw requests. Returned metadata never establishes native custody.

x-owned-sdk-trusted-administration.configuration: A separate Rust AdministrativeClient explicitly selects protected loopback application HTTP provisioning and a signed native status peer with the same supplied credential. It does not discover or fall back to another endpoint, credential or dialect. No ordinary communication/media facade is exposed.
x-owned-sdk-trusted-administration.intent: validate_provisioning bounds and normalizes the current closed schema. Persist the complete command and original unscoped status reference before IO; its logical ID must match MutationOptions. All11 installed command families use their existing documented HTTP routes and server ledger.
x-owned-sdk-trusted-administration.ownership: At most16 active/queued submissions, one owned bounded HTTP transaction. Unwritten cancelled/expired commands are skipped. Losing a caller wait after submission preserves original-ID uncertainty while the HTTP worker finishes; independent signed status remains usable. No hidden mutation retry occurs.
x-owned-sdk-trusted-administration.recovery: Operation<Value> completion checks the exact recorded command_type and provisioning outcome kind/IDs/counters. Saved references query current authorized original receipts without resubmission. An absent/inaccessible unscoped source may be refused; refusal never proves no prior effect. Preserve original intent/ID. Exact intent replay retains its record; changed intent and lost current administrator/target permission refuse. Completion does not confer native media custody.
x-owned-sdk-trusted-administration.cleanup: close stops and joins the application and native owners, clears unwritten work and retains join handles across local cleanup cancellation/timeouts. Input/result Debug output is redacted. Remote HTTP, package/external and operating-profile acceptance remain explicit later qualification.

x-native-reliable-data-sdk.transport: Signed current owned native physical peer only; HTTP submission remains explicitly unsupported (501). Current operation.get and cancellation remain available.

formats.binary: application/octet-stream with canonical base64 body encoding

x-native-reliable-data-sdk.sdk: Stream.send_data preserves caller message and operation IDs; data_send saved references have full Connection scope and are distinct from conversation message_send. Fresh authorized recovery observes admission without owning a native Stream. Signed incoming message.send names the receiver local Stream label; exact owned scope, format, direction and addressed Participant are checked before queueing.
x-native-reliable-data-sdk.queues: At most32 messages per receiving Stream,256 messages and1MiB decoded body bytes overall. Local overflow clears and fails that binding with ResyncRequired; new binding generation/format is needed to reset it. Other control and Streams remain usable. The physical signaling reader has its separate bounded framing queue and terminal transport errors remain explicit.
x-native-reliable-data-sdk.lifecycle: Clones consume one shared ordered queue. Local receive cancellation/deadline consumes no message. A submitted send cancellation preserves original uncertainty; status/replay never creates another logical send. Ended/changed bindings refuse or discard old-generation queued bodies; close wakes receivers and clears queues.

x-native-selection-result.transport: Native receive routing is applied only by the current signed physical owner; HTTP may inspect the original operation.
x-native-selection-result.recovery: Preserve original command, logical ID, scope and native revision. Match signed preparation and recorded completion before adopting local receive bindings; unavailable capture never invents an empty set or a binding grant.

x-native-subscription-reconciliation.subscription_record_id: Stable original explicit stream.subscribe or stream.unsubscribe record that authorized this server-created operation; available while Preparing and preserved through completion or uncertain recovery. Private engine plans are never exposed.
x-native-subscription-reconciliation.authority: Current-authorized operation.get only. Parent record identity is not a permission or physical media grant. An owned SDK must verify its original selector, exact current scope, signed preparation and captured completion before adopting new bindings. Owned SDK callbacks use bounded current-journal reads, original selector identity and matching captured completion. Local progress distinguishes Recorded from bindings_adopted; the read-only stream_reconcile operation kind preserves original recovery. Routing-only journal hints trigger fresh authorized reads before counter synchronization. Exact predecessor counters can advance without optional binding capture when the recorded operation proves no physical change; unavailable resource-replacement capture still requires explicit physical reconciliation.

x-native-routing-journal-hints.transport: Unsolicited signed operation.updated on the original confirmed native physical writer, exact cid/sid/connid/operation_id and no in_reply_to or expected_revision header. Metadata only; never result or bindings. HTTP cannot request this delivery or acquire native ownership.
x-native-routing-journal-hints.ordering: Only after durable completed routing-only stream.reconcile. Per-writer metadata coalesces the latest native revision with at most64 queued Connections. Pending IO reacquires exact current owner, selector, generation, Device, Endpoint, key and membership permission at the actual writer; no idle reader is queued. Incomplete reliable output retires before its reader releases.
x-native-routing-journal-hints.client: A hint is never authorization or completion evidence. The owned SDK verifies its original selector, performs current operation.get and matches announced immutable IDs/counters before applying a captured observation. Unsettled preparation recovery cannot be overwritten. Null captures only advance an exact installed predecessor when the journal proves no physical resources changed.
x-native-routing-journal-hints.recovery: One bounded observation job per owned Connection shares explicit command capacity and original deadlines. Stale/foreign/unissued/malformed hints cannot acquire custody. Hint delivery is advisory; durable journal/cursor catch-up and wider backpressure profiles remain separate qualification.

x-native-runtime-controls.transport: Signed current original native QUIC peer only; HTTP may inspect/cancel the operation but cannot apply a native runtime gate.
x-native-runtime-controls.selection: hold/resume select an optional exact streams list, defaulting to all current bindings. mute/unmute require a nonempty exact streams list. All lists are bounded to32 unique logical Stream IDs.
x-native-runtime-controls.semantics: Default hold permits endpoint receive only. hold details.direction may select endpoint sendonly, recvonly or inactive. resume clears hold/pause while preserving independent source mute. mute/unmute change endpoint publication without changing its receive route or hold state.
x-native-runtime-controls.authority: Current connection.update plus original source/Device/key/physical owner and current endpoint/member/recipient authority. The held engine command must match the exact planned action, Stream set, Connection and revision. No negotiation, codec change, new handle or Session role grant.
x-native-runtime-controls.result: An actual returned engine outcome advances stream revision once and records resources_changed:false, action, Connection generation and gate_streams. Observed binding/held directions use the server perspective. readiness_json.last_gate is only the latest bounded partial observation for a matching live generation.
x-native-runtime-controls.recovery: Exact operation replay returns historical outcome without reapplying a gate or resetting newer controls. Captured success retries durable metadata after journal failure without retaining idle readers or repeating Core. Cancellation cannot erase an already committed local control. Historical completion does not revive retirement; successor runtime refuses an old captured receipt.

x-native-quality-configuration.transport: Signed original physical native QUIC peer only; HTTP does not acquire native control authority.
x-native-quality-configuration.completion: A captured actual local configuration result names the original Connection generation, unchanged stream revision and applied quality_interval_ms; resources_changed is false. Media bindings, stream handles and RTP clocks do not change.
x-native-quality-configuration.replay: The complete original payload and expected revision remain immutable. Completed replay returns its original historical receipt without reapplying cadence, including after another operation selects a newer interval. Current authority remains required.
x-native-quality-configuration.recovery: Record a captured success after storage recovery without retaining idle source readers or calling the engine again. Missing actual outcome remains uncertain; never recreate a retired Connection from its saved interval.

x-record-response-profile.custody: Current bearer/source fences and exact record retained through actual socket IO, including copied/buffered Body bytes; deadline bounded by credential expiry; cancellation/retirement abort IO.
x-record-response-profile.larger-views: Optional authenticated HTTPS references; explicit record_delivery_unavailable when no live endpoint is installed.
x-record-response-profile.url-selector: Live server-issued HTTPS URL plus optional condition selects a fresh current authorized view; Conversation/Session/UUID must agree; unknown/expired/foreign URLs are local misses without network IO. GET remains bound to its original view/expiry.

x-native-capability-advertisement.transport: Signed original physical native QUIC peer only; HTTP cannot declare capabilities for a native Connection.
x-native-capability-advertisement.authority: Current original participant/member epoch, Identity, credential/key, Device, Endpoint, runtime generation, stream revision and actual physical owner. A declared assurance label cannot replace or overstate the authenticated assurance.
x-native-capability-advertisement.completion: Descriptor replacement and operation completion commit atomically. The receipt carries the original Connection generation, unchanged stream revision, exact descriptor/participant/trigger and advertisement record. No binding, codec, route or media permission changes.
x-native-capability-advertisement.replay: Original logical intent is immutable. Replay returns its original historical result without replacing a newer descriptor; delayed recording cannot recreate retired media.
x-native-capability-advertisement.future-negotiation: The latest authorized complete declaration governs subsequent explicit codec updates and new stream choices within current Endpoint, Session and local engine limits. Gained codecs require an independent real negotiation; withdrawn formats cannot be newly selected. Existing confirmed bindings and their source selectors remain usable. Original completed replay does not restore an older declaration; prepared requests must match the current declaration generation.

listener-delivery.transport: Unsolicited signed capability.advertise on the exact current recipient native physical writer; cid/sid/connid identify the source, without operation_id or in_reply_to.
listener-delivery.journal: Queue only after durable completion. Pending descriptors coalesce to the latest source declaration; completed replay never republishes.
listener-delivery.audience: Require the original source disclosure audience and current private scene, exact source/recipient lifecycle and credential incarnations, and fresh joint source/recipient Store permission through actual reliable IO.
listener-delivery.custody: Queued items retain metadata only. Actual unfinished reliable sink is retired before fresh source/recipient readers are released; a healthy in-flight frame finishes before a queued replacement.

x-native-capability-advertisement.observation: Server receipt does not confirm delivery to another peer or trigger automatic codec renegotiation. Local listener qualification and unresolved checks are recorded separately in auxiliary-native-capability-delivery.json.

x-movement-completion.authority: Current-authorized original operation reads expose captured local results. Actual preparation, confirmed resources, movement, recording and media remain separate boundaries. Historical completion never adopts another peer or revives a retired target.
x-movement-completion.scope: Native/telephone movement records exact retained/admitted/retired topology alongside actual target and original source. Physical media still requires current route custody.

x-transition-receipt-identity.scope: Native signed transition admission and operation.get carry authoritative original command and stable record identity. The HTTP OperationRecord carries the same original facts. Native SDK restoration verifies the returned command before decoding a transition result.
x-transition-receipt-identity.continuation: A saved typed consultation retains its original via and retained Connection. Return uses the saved host-issued original record ID, reads it under current authority only if not yet observed, and creates a new logical return operation under current host authority. Unknown or cancelled waiting never creates a new consultation.
x-transition-receipt-identity.authority: Retained/admitted/retired topology and remote_continuing are captured observations; no receipt grants physical media custody or proves remote playback.

x-native-codec-observation.transport: Native physical codec mutation requires signed peer custody; HTTP mutation returns501. Current-authorized operation.get exposes its captured historical receipt.
x-native-codec-observation.identities: Native bindings use distinct positive port handles, including reliable data. Data observations do not grant RTP I/O. All Stream IDs in one captured set are unique; native model revision, stream generations and Connection generations are distinct counters.
x-native-codec-observation.grant: A receipt alone cannot install physical ownership or revive a retired generation.

x-native-codec-lifecycle.delivery: Native codec replacement publishes adjacent signed stream.closed and stream.opened observations as one guarded physical-writer batch after confirmed fresh replacement flow.
x-native-codec-lifecycle.timestamps: closed_at preserves the earlier observed retirement time; both envelope ts values identify their common publication.
x-native-codec-lifecycle.authority: One current original-source guard covers both exact old/new bindings through actual IO, with revision/flow/credential checks before every poll. Partial second-write interruption retires the sink before releasing the guard and remains uncertain.
x-native-codec-lifecycle.http: These physical-native observations are not HTTP command responses; the ordinary journal and operation receipt remain authoritative.

x-session-cancel-boundary.state: A fresh session.cancel is permitted only while the Session is invited, before any invitee accepts. After acceptance use session.end; remaining pending invitees do not reopen cancellation.
x-session-cancel-boundary.atomicity: A rejected post-acceptance cancellation preserves accepted and pending appearances and the topology revision.
x-session-cancel-boundary.replay: Exact completed cancellation replay returns its original decision under current receipt authority. A late fresh accept cannot revive the cancelled Session.
x-session-cancel-boundary.native-observation: Within an active bounded server invitation exchange, successful native or HTTP cancellation can emit session.cancel on each exact original native recipient route. in_reply_to is its actual signed forwarded invitation ID; immutable original by/reason values and fresh current recipient/source/key authority govern the reliable write.
x-session-cancel-boundary.native-caller-reference: The signed native cancel_session_invitation helper asserts the original caller invitation wire ID through in_reply_to, with its own logical cancellation operation ID. Exact physical admission and original CID/SID metadata must match before ordinary mutation. Current permission, configured human-consent step-up, source/membership/recipient ceilings and topology checks remain required. Metadata is registered before the invitation ACK and survives only a bounded physical lifetime. Logical invitation replay supplies a fresh current reference after reconnect; the same logical cancellation then recovers its immutable receipt.
x-session-cancel-boundary.limits: Unsigned HTTP rejects native in_reply_to references and uses ordinary logical cancellation with the same current authority and ledger. The journal/snapshot remains authoritative; broader profiles remain assigned.

x-session-end-authority.participants: A current present Session Participant may end the logical Session without session.manage. The authenticated by assertion, current membership epoch, topology revision, original Session source access and all affected recipient ceilings remain required. Pending invitations and departed appearances grant no end authority. Existing creator/explicit manager authority remains available.
x-session-end-authority.replay: Exact operation replay checks current named permission and original source/membership authority and never emits a second terminal fact.

x-session-terminal-observation.wire: Finite conversation.subscribe catch-up includes session.ended before its original cursor-bearing conversation.event. Native live subscriptions use the same original metadata and current source authority.
x-session-terminal-observation.scope: cid/sid identify the ended Session; in_reply_to identifies the subscription request. No connid or operation_id is added to the typed hint.
x-session-terminal-observation.payload: Original ended_at, known by Participant or null, supplied reason_code/reason. Runtime unspecified numeric reasons use0; missing text is unspecified. No provider status is inferred.
x-session-terminal-observation.journal: session_ended data contains the original shared Session snapshot, known actor epoch, reason and time. Independent immutable metadata survives release/retention of a larger vCon record.
x-session-terminal-observation.record: Asynchronous vCon finalization uses separate recording.vcon-ready; a terminal hint does not invent a ready handle or audio capture.
x-session-terminal-observation.authority: Current session_get and original/current Session source access, membership epoch, recipient ceiling and actual query delivery readers remain required.

x-owned-session-invitations.delivery: After a completed ordinary Session invite, a bounded worker forwards the immutable original offer to current authenticated native live routes. No media Connection or Conversation subscription is required. Actual writer custody reacquires one exact current credential/Device/key/source read union.
x-owned-session-invitations.response: A signed session.accept/session.reject observation must match the exact physical waiter, final server wire id, CID/SID and server invitation source correlation. It never enters ordinary command dispatch. A dedicated source decision enforces the same configured human-consent floor, then rechecks the original pending target slot, epochs, current named action, recipient ceiling and physical lifetime before atomic journal/decision commit. No ordinary caller operation is created for a response.
x-owned-session-invitations.limits: Original accept/reject decisions can be relayed to an exact registered native caller under fresh original receipt/epoch/source/key authority; native logical replay re-correlates a stored decision after disconnect. Configured tel:/sip: targets use separately owned gateway authority. Task-origin policy, Linux and remote/browser/provider qualification remain open. A local metadata submission or ACK does not assert recipient acceptance or Connection/media readiness.

x-session-invitation-targets.single-participant: The initiator is implicit. An initial session.invite with to:[] admits one present Participant with accepted capability intent, no outbound invitation and no claim of Active Session or media readiness. Current named permission, membership, Session source and capacity still apply. A fresh invitation on an existing Session requires at least one target; exact original solo replay keeps its initial receipt even after later participants join.
accepted-references: tel: reference to a verified configured current member Endpoint
sip: reference to a verified configured current member Endpoint
x-session-invitation-targets.resolution: Resolve each reference to its current Participant and membership epoch under the same Store resource authority. Gateway selectors require the exact verified Endpoint, unrevoked Device and live installed initial gateway registration; current independent Endpoint/route credentials and configured SIP authority remain required. No implicit Conversation admission, directory-wide discovery or arbitrary URI dialing.
x-session-invitation-targets.authority: The named session.invite permission and current resolved recipient ceiling are required. Removed, revoked, foreign, ambiguous and unadmitted targets refuse; duplicate aliases of one Participant refuse before mutation.
x-session-invitation-targets.replay: Preserve original requested references in the immutable logical intent. Changing an Identity ID to its Participant ID under the same operation ID conflicts; exact replay does not reinvite or rewrite current presence.
x-session-invitation-targets.durable-source: Successful local admission captures immutable inviter/target membership epochs and a current per-target pending slot. Schema99 freezes URI Endpoint ID/revision/address/policy with the invitation. Exact original replay keeps that binding after address reassignment and cannot dial another target; fresh actual IO and media require independent current authority. Registration and protected metadata readers grant no IO.
x-session-invitation-targets.limits: Installed UDP initial gateways support configured tel: and sip: targets. sips: requires a TLS gateway and is explicitly unsupported by this host; other schemes and unconfigured Endpoints refuse. Task-origin policy, wider Linux/browser/remote/provider qualification and the rest of G6-046 remain separate. Installed invitations/decisions do not assert Connection or media readiness.

x-native-flow-facts.scope: Schema92 installation-owned historical native readiness source; no public fact query or mutation command.
x-native-flow-facts.authority: A non-deserializable engine witness captures exact controller/credential revision, confirmed native epoch and direction-appropriate flow under current active port custody. The host reacquires the original current source read independently; the fact never grants IO.
x-native-flow-facts.ordering: The first fact for a Connection generation/runtime is immutable and retained before its connection.ready hint is permitted. Storage failure retries metadata only, with no idle permission reader or extra media submission. Hint output uncertainty cannot rewrite a committed source fact.
x-native-flow-facts.limits: Schema93 atomically starts the accepted/ready Session on its first verified public native flow. Private preparation does not activate a Session. Participant joined/left and loss/reconnect grace remain open. Packet silence is not a Connection loss observation.
x-native-flow-facts.transient-contention: A busy packet metadata registry yields NotReady without claiming source revocation. Native readiness delivery retries a temporarily unavailable current media check with the original physical source and a fresh authority interval. No reader remains held while waiting; missing, poisoned, cancelled or unauthorized source state never grants delivery. Advisory quality defers a busy Store reader. A pre-IO metadata timeout or temporary storage refusal keeps the lifecycle observer registered and recomputes its next hint with fresh authority; quality waits for its next cadence. This does not repeat an actual write or business command. Initial native observer installation retries temporary metadata contention on the already admitted original route within the original offer deadline, without repeating preparation, parameter negotiation, admission or durable ready commit. A lost pre-write lifecycle seal releases all proposal grants before rederiving a hint from the same live original observer and fresh policy. Native stream invocation lookup contention similarly remains authority-busy inside the original command deadline, before any routing effect; missing and poisoned entries remain refusals.

x-session-participant-observations.source: Schema94 distinguishes admitted Session presence from verified public connected presence. First actual public readiness joins an appearance; more Connections do not duplicate it. Pending/replacement Connections preserve the appearance until terminal settlement. Explicit Session leave, removal and confirmed native retirement reconcile departures atomically with their source mutations.
x-session-participant-observations.wire: session.participant.joined contains original participant_id/identity_id/kind/Session role/display_name/joined_at and via_connection. session.participant.left contains original participant_id/left_at and explicit-leave, all-connections-ended, kicked or transferred-out. No connid/operation_id/reply scope on unsolicited native hints.
x-session-participant-observations.ordering: One bounded metadata worker reads durable start/join/left references in source order and independently authorizes every actual recipient writer. No idle media/permission reader; no historical unsolicited replay on startup. Journal catch-up supplies original typed hints before cursor facts.
x-session-participant-observations.identity: Original role/name, membership epoch and via-Connection provenance never change with later labels, duplicate readiness, reconnect, replay or end. Facts do not authorize media or grant history.
x-session-participant-observations.limits: Implementation verification in progress under G6-046. Full Session grace, promotion/restart/loss matrix and browser/SIP/remote qualifications remain separate.

x-session-started.source: Initial activation waits for current observed public native/SIP readiness covering every accepted Participant. Actual native flow and actual owned SIP connected observations qualify their own sources; negotiation and provisional metadata do not. Accepted-set and attributed public-scope changes are reconciled without another packet. Unready scans queue no authority writer.
x-session-started.payload: Original server activation started_at, accepted participants_present, and current ready active_connections with connid/participant_id/transport. SIP uses sip-interop. negotiated_capabilities contains common selected descriptors, with exact per-Connection descriptors when formats differ. Captured current codec bindings supersede the first-flow codec summary. Replay never rewrites the start.
x-session-started.delivery: Bounded native multicast independently reauthorizes each current recipient credential, key, Device, source, membership epoch and recipient ceiling. The physical recipient needs no media Connection of its own. No connid/operation_id/in_reply_to envelope scope.
x-session-started.http: Finite conversation.subscribe catch-up emits the original session.started before its conversation.event with subscription correlation, subject to current source and epoch access.
x-session-started.failure: Storage failure rolls back activation, start snapshot and journal together. Initial SIP connected recording retains its exact admitted leg and retries only metadata within the original bounded deadline, without another SIP call or native packet.
x-session-started.limits: Qualification is local macOS arm64 native QUIC and loopback SIP fixtures. Linux, browser and named remote/provider profiles retain their assigned tasks; no gate acceptance or publication is implied.

x-native-dtmf.transport: dtmf.send requires its original signed physical native QUIC or configured WebTransport peer. HTTP cannot supply native source custody; use operation.get/cancel/reconcile for the existing logical operation.

payload.digits: 1..32 ASCII telephone digits, exact spelling retained
payload.duration_ms: RFC4733 40..6000; INFO100..5000; complete schedule <=30 seconds including70ms gaps
payload.extensions: Preserved as logical retry identity; source/observation claims never supply authenticated provenance.

x-native-dtmf.receipt: operation.updated preparing records original custody. Reconcile the same logical ID for per-recipient local outcomes; ACK is not a playback receipt.
x-native-dtmf.delivery: Signed unsolicited dtmf.received on each exact original/current permitted native recipient writer, with original operation_id, actual source received_at and source=uctp-native. Queues retain metadata; every write needs fresh named source/recipient permission and original/current private audience.
x-native-dtmf.sip-gateways: The same native command may freeze actual initial or committed replacement SIP recipients. Schema102 keeps established recipients under their real telephone lifetime, generation and SIP call identity. Each original schedule independently rechecks current source dtmf.send and destination dtmf.receive; an established route retains sip_dial and its own named signal permission without borrowing the retired native credential. INFO/RFC4733 retries preserve the same original local schedule and actual current physical binding. No media grant or remote playback receipt is implied.
x-native-dtmf.outcome: One actual output frame per frozen recipient. Local outcomes are not_started/local_submitted/outcome_unknown. Completed uses result; other final states use problem.signal. Any possible partial IO stays unknown; replay/restart never resubmits.
x-native-dtmf.private-audience: Initial and committed moved SIP calls retain their actual typed outside-audience lifetime during native private consultation and return. Current route/media reads authorize only unchanged public programmes and private exclusion. No SIP call borrows native signing or initial-call credentials; sealed DTMF observations cannot gain recipients when a private audience returns.
x-native-dtmf.credential-epoch: An observed native auth.refresh preserves Connection and Stream identity. Fresh signals use the applied credential epoch. Frozen recipient registrations and epochs remain original; unstarted old-epoch work is never reassigned to a successor. Reconcile its original operation ID. Refresh cannot renew an original deadline or restart IO.
x-native-dtmf.metadata-admission: Busy Core or native-source metadata defers only the same original sealed source and frozen recipient before writer allocation, at most two seconds and original expiry. No idle permission readers; fresh policy still gates actual IO once. Pre-IO deadline/cancellation records not_started and replay never sends.
x-native-dtmf.partial-io: Destroy the native sink and cancel its physical route before releasing actual IO readers or waking uncertainty. Abort has the same retirement ordering. Definite pre-IO refusal preserves the healthy writer. HTTP status never authorizes resubmission.
x-native-dtmf.qualification: Service integration is in progress under G6-046; runtime evidence is required separately. No remote playback claim.

x-received-sip-dtmf.scope: Schema103 separate trusted SIP source journal with explicit initial or committed telephone lifetime kind. HTTP cannot submit a physical source observation or supply native signing custody.
x-received-sip-dtmf.provenance: Actual sip-info or rfc4733 source ID, receive time, digits, duration and optional original RTP facts are frozen with the actual connected initial or committed replacement SIP incarnation and original native recipients. No native stream revision or signing fields are invented.
x-received-sip-dtmf.authority: Current dtmf.send on the initial source Endpoint or committed source route, and dtmf.receive on each exact native recipient, original/current membership and audience, installed runtime and physical binding remain required at actual IO. Signal permission never grants media.
x-received-sip-dtmf.recovery: Reserve one actual signed native frame ID before IO. A successor records reserved attempts as outcome_unknown and unstarted recipients as not_started, without resubmission. Cancellation and expiry recovery wait for owned physical reads to release.
x-received-sip-dtmf.status: The current original logical participant identity may use operation.get/cancel with current named source and audience permissions. An independent route credential authorizes signal IO but does not become the logical operation owner; frozen recipients do not become owners. Completed results and problem.signal use ReceivedDtmfSubmission; empty audiences record no submission.
x-received-sip-dtmf.qualification: Controlled Store behavior is separate from installed physical receive-to-native delivery qualification under G6-046.

x-user-assurance.policy: Protected server TOML user_assurance rules bind exact Conversation, command and required user_id. The required granular operation follows that command. Policy is immutable for this runtime and shared with signed peers and HTTP.
x-user-assurance.native: Current signed preflight may suspend one original logical mutation and emit identity.step-up-request. Explicit supplied successor must prove the configured user and required scope, preserve Identity/issuer/installation/Device, and have the same separately enrolled signing key. Both credentials and original resource authorization remain current under execution/delivery custody. Original operation/revision are never replaced.
x-user-assurance.http: HTTP commands never initiate native step-up and cannot bypass a configured floor. Supply an already current explicitly consented credential; an ordinary identified bearer is refused.
x-user-assurance.limits: User-authorized consent is implemented separately from task-scoped delegation; canonical ctg1 task grants and owned-audio assurance transitions remain unqualified. Runtime evidence is recorded under G6-046.

get.description: Configured canonical transport metadata through the loopback application listener. Requires a current bearer before bounded body collection. GET body must be empty. Response names configured WebTransport HTTPS and TLS WebSocket WSS mounts or null when disabled, mandatory Origin enforcement, and WebTransport per-session datagram negotiation. WSS control metadata does not assert WebRTC media support. It installs no TLS/signing trust, endpoint verification, authorization, session or media grant. An unrelated HTTP or webhook-only listener cannot advertise a canonical listener. Read-only, no automatic retries, no-store; SDK transport_discovery uses the existing cancellation/deadline/response bounds.

200.description: Configured metadata; at most8192 UTF-8 JSON bytes.

401.description: Current bearer invalid, expired or revoked.

404.description: Canonical transport discovery unavailable on this listener.

post.description: Explicit human consent, authenticated before bounded JSON decoding. The consenting current ordinary credential must have credential.delegate and every requested operation/recipient. User Identity is derived from that credential, never accepted from the body. Target must be current in the same tenant. No wildcards, admin, re-delegation or synthetic assurance label. Issuance atomically persists immutable consent and a narrow successor credential. Exact retry by the original current issuer and operation ID returns the same secret/expiry; changed intent conflicts and revoked/expired authority refuses replay. Enroll the successor Device/signing-key binding separately before native use. Consenting credential/Identity revocation waits for existing delegated subject IO and invalidates every affected successor; independently issued credentials remain independent. No remote publication or provider access is implied.

200.description: Same immutable consent and protected successor secret. Do not log or share the body.

403.description: Human provenance or current operation/recipient/tenant/expiry ceiling denied.

429.description: Active or retained consent capacity exhausted.

503.description: Authority/storage unavailable or acceptance uncertain; retain the original complete request.

get.description: Optional separately bound pinned TLS HTTP/1.1 listener. Authenticate the current bearer before locator lookup; derive fresh explicit record_get, original Session/source access and viewer authority; require the exact record revision, body/manifest binding and projected digest. Tokens hold metadata only and never grant access. Stop/restart invalidates references. Close/no-store response retains guards through actual TLS/socket IO; expiry, cancellation or retirement aborts remaining writes.

200.description: Exact current authorized vCon bytes; maximum 16 MiB.

401.description: Current bearer invalid, expired or revoked.

409.description: Reference expired or its record/projected view changed.

content_hash.description: Digest of these exact authorized projected bytes; never the full source digest for a filtered view.

body.description: Runtime enforces 64 KiB decoded UTF-8/binary bytes, independently of JSON character length.

Envelope.title: Gate 6 UCTP envelope / connect/2 target
Envelope.description: Schema conformance does not establish authorization, active media, provider effects or runtime qualification.

NativeDataAcceptance.description: Historical local Core queue admission for a signed native Connection-scoped message.send. Neither a recipient write nor remote application consumption; operation.get requires current authorization and cannot acquire native custody.

NativeHandoffCompletion.description: Captured topology and optional native role fact. Native participant authority revision, Session topology revision and Conversation revision are distinct. Cleanup pending is historical local progress; this receipt grants no media ownership.

NativeReplacementCompletion.description: Captured committed native/telephone replacement. Retained/admitted/retired IDs are recorded with the move, never inferred from readiness or SDK input. The replaced source is retired, the admitted ID equals connection_id, and all IDs across the three sets are distinct. Generation and membership epoch are observations, not media grants or resource revisions.

NativeCodecBinding.description: Captured binding metadata, never a media grant. All native port handles are distinct positive u16 values, including data ports. An observed data port does not grant RTP I/O; logical Stream IDs stay distinct. Full captured sets contain at most32bindings and32768encoded bytes.

NativeCodecResult.description: Historical direct codec completion or captured Session-policy reconciliation. Binding directions describe the server; SDK parameter observations reverse them for the client. All bindings share one Connection generation. The optional batch reference does not grant physical custody.

NativeSelectionResult.description: Captured original native receive selection. Actual stream revision equals expected or expected+1; a resource change requires expected+1. Bindings are the fenced actual commit observation, null if a concurrent capture was unavailable, and [] only for a known empty set. Positive unique native handles, including data, are private observations. Historical recovery never grants foreign media custody.

url.description: Configured exact HTTPS contact, without credentials/query/fragment/zero port. Install TLS and server-signing trust separately.
Configured exact TLS WebSocket contact. Install TLS and server-signing trust separately; this advertises control only, not WebRTC media readiness.

credential.description: Protected successor secret returned only to the current authenticated consenting issuer.

x-connect-canonical-websocket.enabled: Optional protected canonical server websocket configuration; disabled by default.

configuration.bind: Explicit bounded network-profile TCP listener; separate from the UDP QUIC/WebTransport address.
configuration.mount_path: Exact absolute path, at most256 ASCII bytes without dot segments or double slashes.
configuration.allowed_origins: Between1 and32 unique exact HTTPS origins; explicit loopback HTTP only for Local development. Missing, repeated or different Origin is refused.
configuration.advertised_url: Exact WSS mount; required for Remote. Local omission derives actual bound TCP IPv4/bracketed IPv6 contact.

x-connect-canonical-websocket.authority: The same canonical identity, signed control protocol, current Store authentication/authorization, operation ledger and global physical peer budget as QUIC/WebTransport.
x-connect-canonical-websocket.lifetime: Owned bounded intake and TLS/authentication; server key expiry, shutdown or drop retires active physical peers. WSS and QUIC/WebTransport intake failure retire linked transports.
x-connect-canonical-websocket.media: Control hosting only. WebRTC SDP/ICE/media integration and forced-browser fallback qualification remain G6-051 work.
x-connect-canonical-websocket.recovery: Keep original mutation IDs across uncertainty; observe status using current authority. No automatic mutation retry or transport migration.

x-connect-canonical-webtransport.enabled: Optional protected canonical server webtransport config; disabled by default.
x-connect-canonical-webtransport.profile: connect/2 over HTTP3 h3 on the native TLS endpoint; same identity, canonical handlers, Store and physical budget.

configuration.mount_path: Exact absolute mount path, at most256 ASCII bytes without dot segments or double slashes.
configuration.allowed_origins: Between1 and32 unique exact serialized HTTPS origins. Explicit localhost/loopback HTTP origins are permitted only for Local development. Missing, repeated or nonmatching Origin is refused.
configuration.advertised_url: Exact HTTPS mount contact; required for Remote. Local omission derives the actual bound IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 contact, preserving address family. Fresh Local TLS certificates cover localhost/loopback IP identities; client trust remains explicit. No credentials, query, fragment, whitespace/control characters or zero port.

x-connect-canonical-webtransport.media: The actual authenticated physical transport and current verified Device Endpoint select the registered WebTransport adapter. Offer/reply/reoffer substrate stays bound to that transport. Media resources require actual negotiation; control-only peers cannot allocate new media.
x-connect-canonical-webtransport.replay: Same owner-scoped logical mutation IDs and current authorization. A new transport cannot relabel a retained Endpoint or repeat an uncertain media effect.
x-connect-canonical-webtransport.qualification: G6-049 is in progress. See docs/evidence/gate-6/webtransport-composition.json for scoped results and scoped runtime results and remaining qualification.

x-connect-canonical-mcp.configuration: Optional protected [mcp] configuration on the canonical server; disabled by default. bind must be loopback even for the Remote native profile. Port zero is allowed for isolated fixtures; use a concrete protected address for an installed host.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.transport: Owned separate MCP Streamable HTTP listener at /mcp, using the official RMCP server and MCP 2025-11-25. The CLI reports mcp_streamable_http without secrets. This is not a route on the canonical HTTP/JSON listener.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.authority: Default admission accepts current ordinary Identity credentials and separately registered protected native/host Task grants. Optional binding fixes one registered Native/HostSession origin; provider origins require their verified adapters. Each request reauthorizes. Model arguments never select a credential, actor, signature or physical peer.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.control: Ordinary discovery exposes current finite canonical controls with explicit payload/resource scope and original operation IDs. Typed envelope validation and the shared canonical HTTP service executor enforce protocol floor, assurance, granular resource policy and current response authorization. Named application and Task interfaces keep their own ceilings.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.observations: Canonical reply status/envelopes are retained; a canonical refusal is an MCP structured error. Finite journal reads require live:false and resume after the returned cursor. ACK or completed metadata never proves decoded audio, provider delivery or human action. No live media frames or native offer/answer are tool responses.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.lifetime: The canonical server owns listener startup, readiness and drain/drop. Failed MCP bind unwinds startup and permits installation recovery. Disabled MCP has an explicit unconfigured readiness component.
x-connect-canonical-mcp.qualification: See docs/evidence/gate-6/canonical-mcp-control.json and canonical-mcp-hosting.json for exact local functional scope. Installed actual-model agent-host, live transition/media and remote/provider profiles are separate qualification work.
